bihar_raw_news.title: Nitin Nabin to lead 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao Padyatra' in Bihar and West Bengal today
bihar_raw_news.content: N ew Delhi [India], November 2 (ANI): Bharatiya Janata Party national president Nitin Nabin will lead two major 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao Padyatras' in Bihar and West Bengal on Monday, as part of the party's nationwide campaign against the Opposition's misinformation, disinformation and organised anarchy. Advertisement Nabin's first padyatra will commence at 11:00 AM from Lajpat Park in Bhagalpur, Bihar, and conclude at Seva Jyoti Chowk at 12:30 PM. Thereafter, the BJP National President will travel to Kolkata, West Bengal, where the 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao Padyatra' will commence at 3:00 PM from College Street. The padyatra will conclude at Dharmatala at 5:30 PM. According to an official release, the campaign of the Bharatiya Janata Party is a movement against the lies, deception, conspiracies and anarchy being spread by a desperate and disillusioned Opposition. With the resolve of 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao', every BJP karyakarta is reaching out to villages and households to expose the Opposition's false and fabricated narrative and apprise the people of the truth. Senior party leaders, State BJP presidents, and thousands of dedicated karyakartas are expected to participate in these padyatras being organised on Monday in Bhagalpur, Bihar, and Kolkata, West Bengal. Earlier on Sunday, leading a massive 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' (Save Democracy, Eradicate Anarchy) padyatra in Rohtak, Haryana, Nitin Nabin launched a scathing attack on Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and the Congress over the 1984 anti-Sikh riots and the 'Chalo Delhi' march to Ramlila Maidan. Addressing a large gathering of party workers and citizens at D-Park in Model Town following a march from Chhotu Ram Polytechnic Ground, Nabin slammed the Congress-led INDIA Bloc for organising protests on the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots. He accused Congress of attacking democratic institutions out of frustration over electoral rejection, fostering dynastic rule, and undermining constitutional norms while posing as defenders of the Constitution. During the march, Nabin, along with other party leaders, paid homage at the statue of Mahatma Gandhi. Addressing the gathering, he questioned why the Congress had not apologised to the Sikh community for the 1984 violence and criticised Rahul Gandhi for participating in the Opposition's protest in Delhi. "The Congress party ought to have sought atonement for the sacrifices of them (Sikhs) forced upon people, the massacres, and the killings that took place; they should have offered an apology. Yet, today, they have taken to the streets to protest. I ask, on behalf of the people in this democracy, Rahul Gandhi: when our Sikh brethren were being slaughtered, when a full-scale massacre was unfolding, your father remarked that 'when a big tree falls, the earth shakes.' Because of that 'shaking of the earth,' the lives of so many of my Sikh brothers were extinguished. You should have felt remorse for this; you should have apologised," Nabin said. (ANI)

New Delhi: Independent MLCs Bansidhar Brijwasi, who won from Tirhut graduates' constituency, and Rahul Raj , who won from Saran teachers' constituency, joined BJP in the presence of senior party leaders on Saturday. Bihar BJP chief Sanjay Saraogi's social media post also mentioned that the two leaders have taken the party's membership. The Opposition termed their move a violation of the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution. It stated that an independent MLC cannot join any party; doing so will lead to the disqualification of their membership. Read more: Bihar MLC polls: RJD's Anil Jha declared elected, party's overall tally climbs to 17 "Two independents, Rahul Raj and Bansidhar Brijwasi , joined BJP on Saturday. They even displayed their joining slip to the media. This is a clear violation of the Tenth Schedule and Article 191(2) of the Constitution. RJD would approach the Chairman of the Bihar Legislative Council , seeking the disqualification of the two independent MLCs. The ball is now in the Chairman's court. We would also move the court for justice," RJD leader Manoj Jha told ET. Live Events Realising the faux pas, Brijwasi later said that he had not taken BJP membership, but had only extended support to it. Saraogi also deleted his social media post and replaced it with a new one, stating that the two independent MLCs had extended their support to BJP. "There is no question of them joining the party. They came to BJP office and we welcomed them. They have extended their support to BJP. There is nothing wrong with that. Independent MP Pappu Yadav shares stage with Congress. Has he joined Congress? There is no such issue," Sarogi told ET. Jan Suraaj of Prashant Kishor has also decided to approach the court with an appeal to disqualify the MLCs. Add as a Reliable and Trusted News Source Add Now!
